text.p: Italian bond futures held to lower level in late afternoon with operators taking profits after the lira showed a slightly easier tone, dealers said.

The market had started lower in line with easier bunds this morning but while the German market recovered into positive territory, BTP trading was held back by a lack of enthusiasm to push the market any higher.
The Finnish markka's weekend link to the ERM put investors on the defensive as they contemplated when the lira might enter the European currency grid.
Little direction came from Treasuries in the U.S. where markets were partially closed for the Columbus Day holiday.
Dealers said that they expected that the Italian government would not be knocked off its planned course of looking to enter the ERM when its 1997 budget had passed through parliament.
"There is still a lot of progress to be made on the lira's entry into the ERM, especially working out an entry rate," said one LIFFE trader.
Italy's European partners, especially France, are likely to push for a strong lira entry level while Italy's concern over export levels will push it towards wanting a weaker level.
